jobs.goal: The Bash hook gates commits without rewriting commands
jobs.brief: hooks/register.tsx:328 puts a git() shell function in front of every Bash command whose text contains the word "commit" (gated(), line 107). Auto mode reviewed the original command, sees a different one, and gives no verdict, so calls have to be sent again; harmless commands like `grep commit` are rewritten too. Instead: a parser in hooks/shell.ts (beside movesClaims etc.) finds whether the command runs `git commit` and in which directory (`git -C dir commit`, `cd dir && git commit`, global options skipped as gated() does today). If it does, the hook runs `gmod gate-commit --dir <dir>` itself before next(): a refusal becomes deny with the gate's text, a pass runs the command exactly as written. Every other command runs unchanged. Remove gated(). Not in scope: commits hidden inside scripts or make targets (the shell function caught those; a git pre-commit hook could later), and the Edit/Write guards, which never rewrite.

done_when.text: a command that only mentions commit, or runs no git commit, reaches the shell exactly as written
git commit and git -C <dir> commit run the commit gate in the hook for that dir: a refusal denies the call, a pass runs the command unchanged
a command that runs git commit and also anything but cd and git (an edit, eval, a function) is refused, so what is committed is what the gate saw

jobs.goal: Approving works from any branch, even a job's
jobs.brief: approve (lib/core.mjs:1186) writes .gmod/plan.json and commits it on the checked-out branch, so it refuses a gmod/ job branch (line 1191); adr accept does the same (lib/adr.mjs:145). A person approving from a session that is working a job (its folder on gmod/<job>, or a job worktree) is refused every time. Instead, build the decision commit off the checkout: on main's tip (local main, or origin/main when that is ahead), with a temporary index (read-tree, hash-object, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree), and hand that commit to publishDecision (lib/ci.mjs:591), which today pushes HEAD, so it pushes the given commit as gmod/plan-<sha> / the decision branch. The proposal's base is checked against the plan in that main commit, not the job branch's copy. The checkout, its index and its branch are never touched; when the checkout is on main itself, it still moves to the new commit as today. test/cli.test.mjs ('the agent drafts the plan, a person approves it, and it lands alone', line ~429) asserts that approve on a job's branch is refused; rewrite that part so approve on a job's branch succeeds and leaves the checkout alone, keeping its approve-from-main path. Not in scope: the pane's wording, and plan branches other than main.

done_when.text: approve on a job's branch commits the plan on main's tip, publishes it, and leaves the checkout, index and branch as they were
approve on main behaves as before
adr accept on a job's branch works the same way

jobs.goal: Subagent prompts are never changed by gmod's hook
jobs.brief: hooks/register.tsx ~line 336: in a governed repository, an Agent call whose prompt lacks FOR_SUBAGENTS gets it appended (next({ ...e, prompt: e.prompt + FOR_SUBAGENTS })). Auto mode reviewed the original prompt, sees a changed one and gives no verdict, so the call has to be sent again. Instead, deny such a call with a message that says the subagent needs gmod's routine and quotes FOR_SUBAGENTS to add to the prompt verbatim; a prompt that already carries it passes unchanged, as today. Ungoverned repositories: unchanged. With this and bash-hook-no-rewrite, no gmod hook changes a tool call's input. Not in scope: the routine's wording.

done_when.text: in a governed repository, an Agent prompt without the routine is refused with the routine to add, and nothing runs
a prompt that carries the routine, or any Agent call in an ungoverned repository, runs exactly as written

jobs.goal: A commit bundled with file changes is refused
jobs.brief: bash-hook-no-rewrite landed (PR #17) before its third criterion's code, when the npx check let its gate pass: the commit gate now runs in the hook before the command, so `echo x >> f && git commit -am x` commits what the gate never saw. Add commitsAlone(cmd) to hooks/shell.ts: a command that runs git commit may beside it only cd/pushd/popd and git add/commit/status/diff/log/show/rev-parse, with no redirection into a file and no $(…) beyond cat/printf (heredoc messages); a commit inside eval, sh/bash -c, xargs, source or a shell function is refused. The hook denies such a command with 'a commit runs on its own' before gating. The reader keeps heredoc bodies as one word and reads 2>&1 / &> as redirections. The code is written on gmod/bash-hook-no-rewrite (PR #23, refused because that job is done); carry it over.

done_when.text: a command that runs git commit and also anything but cd and quiet git (an edit, eval, sh -c, a function) is refused before it runs

jobs.goal: One stamp moves whenever anything a surface shows changes
jobs.brief: New lib/stamp.mjs: a counter in <git-common-dir>/gmod/stamp, bumped (write temp file, rename) by every gmod write a signal or state depends on: proposal save/approve/reject, ADR draft save/accept/reject, check runs (evidence), claim, release, and syncClaims/syncMain when they move a ref. stamp(root) returns "<counter>-<hash8>", the hash over the tips of main (local and origin) and every refs/gmod/* from one for-each-ref, so a plain git fetch moves it too. `gmod stamp` prints it (fast: no plan read, no board); state --json and signals --json carry it as `stamp`; capabilities lists `stamp` in commands. Additive to protocol v1.

done_when.text: drafting a job, recording a check run, and claiming each change gmod stamp; reading state or signals does not

jobs.goal: Every clone sees the same plan proposal
jobs.brief: Move the proposal from <git-common-dir>/gmod/proposal.json to refs/gmod/proposal: a commit (gmod identity, empty parents or the previous version as parent) whose tree holds proposal.json. New lib/shared.mjs holds the ref read/write/push helpers the next jobs reuse. Writes push with --force-with-lease on the tip they read; a lost race fetches, re-applies the same edit, and retries a few times, never overwriting. Approve and reject delete the ref locally and on origin. Reading fetches refs/gmod/proposal alongside claims (one fetch). An existing proposal.json from 1.6 is migrated to the ref on first read. No remote: the ref is local only. lib/receive.mjs (Gitea pre-receive) lets refs/gmod/proposal move, unlike claims.

done_when.text: a job drafted in one clone shows in another clone's proposal after a read

jobs.goal: Every clone sees the same ADR drafts
jobs.brief: Move ADR drafts from <git-common-dir>/gmod/adr-drafts.json to one ref per draft, refs/gmod/adr-drafts/<slug>, using lib/shared.mjs. One ref each, so drafts never contend. Accept and reject delete the ref locally and on origin. Reads fetch refs/gmod/adr-drafts/* in the same fetch as claims and the proposal: that fetch lives in syncClaims in lib/core.mjs (SHARED_NAMES), so core gains the adr-drafts refspec and reconciles each draft ref. An existing adr-drafts.json from 1.6 is migrated on first read. lib/receive.mjs lets these refs move (it already passes every ref outside refs/gmod/claims/).

The gate (gmod verify, ci/) never reads them: a test proves verify's result is the same with a forged green runs ref.

jobs.goal: Any surface can decide with one command, people only
jobs.brief: New lib/decide.mjs and `gmod decide <signal-id> <action> [--rev r] [--note text] [--via surface] [--json]`. Finds the signal by id; refuses an action not in its actions. proposal: approve | ask-changes (stores the note on the shared proposal for the agent, as the pane's Ask for changes does) | reject; --rev must match or it refuses (changed since seen). ADR draft: accept | reject. unstick signals: does nothing, answers with the command to run. Only a person: refuse under gmod's agent identity (isAgent) or an agent environment (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CODEX_* , PI_AGENT, GMOD_AGENT, CI); with a TTY, ask the person to type the signal id back; without one, require --via. Plan, ADR and managed decision commits get `Decided-By: <who>` and `Decided-Via: <cli|pane|skiff|…>` trailers (approve and adr accept too). hooks/shell.ts treats `gmod decide` as a person's decision, like approve. capabilities lists decide. docs/limits.md says plainly what the agent check can't stop.

jobs.goal: No empty plan proposals, and a clear word if one exists
jobs.brief: Two rough edges in lib/core.mjs found landing the 1.7 plan. (1) describeProposal calls draft(), which starts a fresh proposal when none is pending, so describing after an approve leaves an empty proposal behind: refuse instead ("there is no proposal to describe"). (2) approve on a proposal that changes nothing runs git commit on an unchanged plan and fails with a raw git error ("git commit -q -m plan: no change"): refuse before writing, with "the proposal changes nothing: reject it", and the proposal card/signal offers reject only (ready is false for an empty diff).

jobs.goal: The hook refuses git and gmod commands, not text
jobs.brief: Seen in Skiff on 1.7.0: agents were refused for edits in their own job's files and then redid them with Edit. (a) movesClaims in hooks/shell.ts matches the whole command: any mention of the shared refs plus the word push, tag or replace anywhere is refused (a sed whose new text mentions them, a python heredoc about git ls-remote, even a script that only imports shell.ts). Read it like decision(): a git command (optionally -C dir) whose subcommand is update-ref, push, branch -D, tag or replace, with an argument under the shared refs, also through sh -c/eval as decision() does. (b) decision() still reads backticks and $(...) inside a quoted heredoc body, so a doc written with cat > a.md <<'EOF' that shows a decide command in backticks is refused; a quoted heredoc's body is text. An unquoted heredoc's $(...) does run, so it stays read, as does a shell reading the heredoc (sh <<EOF). Refusal wording unchanged.

done_when.text: text that mentions the shared refs with push, tag or replace (sed text, a heredoc, a comment, git ls-remote) runs; git push, update-ref, branch -D, tag or replace on them is still refused, also through sh -c

jobs.goal: A released job's branch doesn't block the next claim
jobs.brief: Seen in Skiff: an agent claimed decide-frames in its worktree, released it and stopped, leaving gmod/decide-frames checked out there. The next agent's claim worked but couldn't switch to the branch, so gmod commit pushed from worktree-agent-... and opened PR #51 from it. Fix both ends in lib/core.mjs: release, in a worktree on gmod/<job> with nothing uncommitted, switches it off the branch (to main's tip, detached in a linked worktree) and deletes the branch when it has no commits beyond main; with commits or uncommitted changes it leaves both and says so. claim, when gmod/<job> is checked out in another worktree, says which one and how to free it (gmod release there, or git worktree remove) instead of carrying on from the wrong branch.

done_when.text: after release in a clean worktree, the job's branch is no longer checked out there, and is deleted when it has no commits; a branch with commits or uncommitted work stays

jobs.goal: A landed proposal is dropped, never pushed back
jobs.brief: Seen twice in Skiff on 1.7.1 (pane approve): after approving, refs/gmod/proposal came back locally and on origin, pointing at the very draft just approved (same sha), and the pane showed "no changes" with ".gmod/plan.json changed since this was drafted". Reproduced: when a stale local copy of the approved draft is left behind (no tracking copy), the next sync's reconcile takes it for an offline edit and publishes it. Which process leaves the local copy isn't pinned down, so fix it from the data in lib/core.mjs: a proposal whose plan equals the plan on disk while its base is an older plan has landed. syncClaims drops it after reconciling (unpublish: here and on origin, refusing on a race as now), and proposal() treats it as absent, so the pane, signals and approve never show or act on it. A fresh or unchanged draft (base equal to the current plan) is untouched.

done_when.text: after an approve, a stale local copy of the approved draft is dropped by the next sync, here and on origin, instead of being pushed

jobs.goal: An agent asks the person; the answer comes back
jobs.brief: New lib/requests.mjs (E5 in Skiff's brief). `gmod ask <text> [--options '<json list>']` raises a request for the job claimed here, stored like a proposal (ADR 0002) at refs/gmod/requests/<id> through lib/shared.mjs: {id, job, question, options, by, at, answer?, answeredBy?, answeredAt?, resolved?}; id from the cause (job + question + at), stable on every clone. Add 'requests/' to SHARED_NAMES in lib/core.mjs so sync fetches, reconciles and prunes them, and every write bumps the stamp. `gmod requests [--json] [--job <id>] [--all]` lists open ones, and with --all the answered and resolved ones too, each with question, answer, who answered and when, so a fresh agent on the job (Skiff restarts its worker with the answer) can read it afterwards; answered requests stay until the job is done. lib/signals.mjs: an open request is a 'decide' signal {cause: {request: id}, rev, question, detail: options} with actions ['answer', 'resolve']. lib/decide.mjs: `gmod decide <id> answer --note <text>` records the person's answer (refused without --note, or with an answer not among the options when there are options), `resolve [--note]` closes it without one; person-only rules as for approve. The asking worktree's `gmod notice` (lib/core.mjs) says the answer once, on the agent's next tool round: "gmod: the person answered your question … : <answer>". Answered or resolved requests leave signals; the sweep drops refs of done jobs. lib/capabilities.mjs lists ask and requests.

done_when.text: gmod ask raises a request for the claimed job that every clone sees as a signal with a stable id, a rev, and actions answer and resolve
gmod decide answer and resolve close it, answer only by a person and only from the options when there are some, and the asking worktree's notice gives the answer once
after it is answered, gmod requests --json --all on any clone still shows the question, the answer, who answered and when, until the job is done

jobs.goal: The person can set a stuck job's signal aside
jobs.brief: A red/stuck job's signal (and a moved job's) gets the action 'resolve': the person fixed it by hand or knows. `gmod decide <id> resolve [--note]` records a shared mark at refs/gmod/resolved/<signal-id> holding the signal's rev; signals hides a signal while its rev equals the mark's. The stuck signal's rev comes from what makes it stuck (its latest failing verdict: head, failing criteria, at), so a new red run or a new main shows it again. Marks are dropped by the sweep once the job is done. Add 'resolved/' to SHARED_NAMES. Person-only like every decide.

done_when.text: resolve hides a stuck job's signal on every clone until it is red again on a new run, and only a person can resolve

jobs.goal: The person re-briefs a stuck job in one decision
jobs.brief: Part of E6. On a stuck or moved job's signal, `gmod decide <id> rebrief --note <new brief>` replaces that job's brief in .gmod/plan.json as the person's decision: committed alone like an approve (`plan: rebrief <job>` with Decided-By/Decided-Via; from a job's branch through decideOnMain, opening its plan PR unless --no-pr), no proposal needed. It refuses a done job, an empty note, and a pending proposal that changes the same job; that refusal names the proposal in the way (its headline or summary, who drafted it, and its signal id) and says to approve or reject it first. It releases the job's claim here and on origin, whoever holds it, so the next worker starts fresh from the new brief. Person-only. The gate already lands a plan-only commit.

done_when.text: decide rebrief commits only the new brief as the person's decision and frees the job's claim; it is refused for a done job, an empty note, or under an agent
while a pending proposal changes the same job, rebrief is refused with a message naming that proposal and its signal id

phases.title: Fixes
phases.outcome: Setting up and running gmod on GitHub works without hand edits or a person approving each run.

phases.title: Contract for faces
phases.outcome: A face like Skiff can read gmod's version, state and signals as JSON, without the pane.

phases.title: Managed mode
phases.outcome: A repository can opt into managed features (for faces like Skiff) with one switch; without it, gmod behaves exactly as before.

phases.title: Managed guard
phases.outcome: Only a person can switch managed mode, and the switch's own pull request lands through the gate.

phases.title: Upkeep
phases.outcome: CI runs gmod 1.6.0, and gmod's hook refuses only real decisions, not commands that mention them.

phases.title: Surfaces contract
phases.outcome: Every surface (pane, CLI, CI, Skiff, Linear, other agents) can watch one stamp, see the same shared proposals, drafts and red jobs under the same signal ids, and decide through gmod decide.

phases.title: Release 1.7
phases.outcome: gmod 1.7.0 is released once, with the whole contract, and this repository's CI runs it.

phases.title: 1.7 follow-ups
phases.outcome: Small fixes to 1.7 from real use: pane decisions say they came from the pane, tests pass with signing on, the hook refuses commands not text, a stale mod says to restart, and a released branch frees the next claim.

phases.title: Release 1.7.1
phases.outcome: gmod 1.7.1 is released with the five follow-up fixes, and CI runs it.

phases.title: Landed proposals
phases.outcome: An approved proposal never comes back as a stale "no changes" card, and 1.7.2 ships the fix.

phases.title: Requests and decisions
phases.outcome: An agent can ask the person a question and get the answer back, and the person can resolve or re-brief a stuck job, from the pane, the CLI or Skiff.

phases.title: Setup and doctor
phases.outcome: A person's surface like Skiff can set a repository up in one call and read back exactly what is set up, as JSON.

phases.title: Release 1.8
phases.outcome: gmod 1.8.0 is released with requests, resolve, re-brief, setup --json and doctor --json, Skiff has fixtures for each, and CI runs it.

phases.title: Lean status
phases.outcome: An agent's mcp__gmod__status returns what it needs to work (its claim and the open jobs) in a few thousand tokens, however long the plan's history grows.
